cards.def: The Jacksonian idea that every man should have an equal chance to rise, not that wealth, talent, or condition should be made equal.
The old system in which the Republican congressional caucus chose the party's presidential nominee, condemned as undemocratic.
The charge that Henry Clay swung the House to John Quincy Adams in exchange for being named secretary of state.
The party that formed around Clay and Adams after the 1824 election, and later gave way to the Whigs.
The party of Jackson's supporters, uneasy about the market, hostile to monopolies and the national bank, and in favor of limited government and equality of opportunity for white men.
The party organized from National Republicans and Anti-Masons, comfortable with the market and favoring Clay's American System of tariff, bank, and internal improvements.
A movement that attacked Freemasonry as a secret, aristocratic order, pioneered the national nominating convention, and later fed members into the Whig Party.
The national rivalry of Democrats and Whigs that replaced the first party system and then dominated American politics.
The dropping of property qualifications so that most adult white men could vote, the core democratic reform of the 1820s and 1830s.
A party meeting that chose presidential candidates in place of the congressional caucus, first pioneered by the Anti-Masons.
The practice of giving public offices to political supporters, which Jackson defended as "rotation in office" to prevent an entrenched bureaucracy.
The law that authorized moving eastern Indian nations west of the Mississippi.
The forced march of the Cherokees west, on which about one-quarter died.
The Supreme Court ruling that Indian tribes had full authority over their lands and that Georgia could not extend its laws over them.
Calhoun's theory that a state convention could void a federal law that exceeded Congress's powers, and that the state might secede if a constitutional amendment then bound it.
The protective tariff that South Carolina assailed as an unfair tax and answered with the Exposition and Protest.
The paper, later revealed to be by Vice President John C. Calhoun, that set out the theory of nullification.
The law giving the president military powers to collect federal tariffs in a defiant state.
The package in which a lower tariff and the Force Bill were signed the same day, and South Carolina repealed its nullification ordinance.
Jackson's doctrine, in his Proclamation on Nullification, that the Union had no right of secession and could not be dissolved by a state.
The demand that wages and payments be made in gold and silver only, not in depreciated state banknotes.
The selected state banks, mostly Democratic, that received federal deposits after Jackson removed them from the Second Bank.
Jackson's order that the government accept only gold and silver for public land, issued after a frantic land boom.
Henry Clay's program of a protective tariff, a national bank, and federal internal improvements, embraced by the Whigs.
The organization, founded by men including Henry Clay, that sought to send free African Americans to Africa and founded Liberia.
Popular northern entertainments in which white actors in blackface caricatured African Americans as unable to handle freedom.

cards.term: Charles River Bridge v. Warren Bridge
cards.def: The Taney Court ruling that struck down implied monopolies and held that the public interest outweighed a corporate privilege, promoting competition.
